# HAE (Haemonetics Corporation) — Technical Analysis Report
**As of 2026-10-07 | Close: $101.71**

## Executive Summary

HAE is in a corrective downtrend within a much larger structural uptrend. The stock staged an explosive re-rating on 2026-08-18 (gap from ~$90 to ~$104.65, on volume of 2.3M — roughly 4x the typical ~500–700K daily volume), rallied to a peak zone of ~$109.5 in mid-to-late September, and has since bled lower for two straight weeks. Price now sits on the lower Bollinger Band and just above the rising 50-day SMA — a decision point, not a confirmed breakdown.

## Trend Structure

**Long-term: Strongly bullish.** Close of $101.71 vs. 200-day SMA of $75.37 — the stock trades ~35% above its long-term mean, and the 50-day SMA ($100.26) is far above the 200-day, confirming a well-established bull regime. The entire move since July has been an up-leg: from ~$75 on 2026-07-01 to $101.71 today (+~36% over the period, based on verified closes in the dataset).

**Medium-term: Correcting.** After the 2026-08-18 gap-up, price ground higher into a ~$108–110 plateau (highs of $109.57 on 2026-08-20, $110.45 on 2026-09-18, $110.28 on 2026-09-23). Since 2026-09-22, however, every rally has been sold: closes stepped down from $108.52 (9/22) to $101.71 (10/07), the weakest close since 2026-09-01 ($101.95).

**Short-term: Bearish momentum, accelerating into support.** The 10-EMA ($104.41) is now above price and falling, and price closed below it every day this week. On 2026-10-07 the stock closed near its session low ($101.32 low vs. $101.71 close) — a sign sellers controlled the tape into the close.

## Indicator Detail

**MACD / Histogram:** MACD line sits at +0.84 but the signal line is at +1.81 — MACD has been below signal since ~2026-09-18, and the histogram (-0.97) is at its most negative reading since mid-September. Momentum is decisively to the downside, though still in positive territory, meaning this is a momentum decay within an uptrend, not yet a trend flip.

**RSI:** At 42.28, RSI has fallen from overbought readings above 70 (9/17–9/22) through the midline. It's neutral-bearish — no oversold condition yet (30 is far away), so momentum offers no natural reversal trigger here.

**Bollinger Bands:** Price ($101.71) is hugging the lower band ($101.26) while the mid-band ($105.49) and upper band ($109.71) sit far above. Band width has compressed dramatically from ~$28 (early September) to ~$8.5 — the early-October range was a volatility contraction, and today's sell-off is the directional resolution of that squeeze, so far to the downside.

**50-day SMA:** $100.26 and rising ~$0.4–0.55/day. This is the line in the sand: the 50-day has risen uninterrupted through this entire dataset and has never been tested since the August breakout. A close below ~$100 would break the medium-term trend structure.

**ATR:** 2.64 — about 2.6% of price. Volatility is near its recent lows after the September chop; a single ATR move covers the entire distance to the 50-day SMA.

## Actionable Observations

- **Key support cluster: $100–101.3.** The lower Bollinger Band ($101.26), today's low ($101.32), and the 50-day SMA ($100.26) stack into a ~$1 zone. How price behaves here determines the next leg.
- **Bullish case:** Holding the $100–101 zone while the histogram stops expanding negatively would set up a mean-reversion trade back toward the mid-band (~$105.5). RSI at 42 gives room for a bounce without needing oversold conditions.
- **Bearish case:** A close below $100 (below the 50-day SMA with ATR room to run) opens a measured move toward the early-September consolidation floor ~$101–102 already broken, then toward the pre-gap region. The gap from 2026-08-18 was never filled — the zone below ~$102.0 was crossed in a single gap, leaving little technical support until much lower.
- **Resistance:** ~$104.4–105.5 (10-EMA and Bollinger mid), then ~$109–110 (upper band / September plateau highs at $110.28–110.45).
- **Risk sizing:** With ATR at 2.64, a stop just below $99.7 (50-SMA minus ~0.2 ATR) risks ~2 points for longs targeting the mid-band — roughly 1:2 reward/risk to $105.5.
- **Volume nuance:** Today's decline came on 625K shares — only average volume, not climactic selling. That argues this is drift, not capitulation; a genuine capitulation day on 1.5M+ shares would more likely mark a low.

## Key Points

| Item | Level / Reading | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Close (10/07) | $101.71 | Near session low; sellers in control short-term |
| Long-term trend | Above 200 SMA ($75.37) by ~35% | Structurally bullish |
| Medium trend | 50 SMA $100.26, rising | Key support ~$100; untested since August |
| Short-term | Below 10 EMA ($104.41) | Bearish; rallies into $104–105.5 are sellable until reclaimed |
| MACD | 0.84 vs signal 1.81; hist -0.97 | Momentum deteriorating, still positive |
| RSI | 42.28 | Neutral-bearish; no oversold signal yet |
| Bollinger | LB $101.26 / Mid $105.49 / UB $109.71 | Price pinned to lower band after squeeze resolution |
| ATR | 2.64 | ~2.6% daily range; use for stops/sizing |
| Support | $101.3–$100.0; then thin zone below | Loss of $100 breaks medium-term structure |
| Resistance | $104.4–105.5; $109–110 | Mid-band and September plateau |
| Volume | 625K on the down day | Distribution, not capitulation |
| Bias | Cautiously bearish short-term, bullish above $100 | Watch $100–101.3 cluster for reversal or break |

# HAE (Haemonetics Corporation) — Fundamentals Report
Point-in-time: 2026-10-07. All figures USD millions, as filed with SEC EDGAR on or before that date.

## Scope note
The fundamentals/profile vendor withheld point-in-time profile data (market cap, multiples, 52-week range, sector/name as of 2026-10-07) and insider transactions could not be dated to filing-publication, so both are excluded. This report is built entirely from as-filed quarterly statements — no look-ahead data.

## Company profile
Haemonetics (HAE) is a medical-technology company in blood and plasma collection/processing (plasma collection devices, hospital hemostasis/vascular products). Revenue ~$1.3B annualized as of mid-2026.

## Income statement — recent quarters

| Period | Revenue | Gross Profit | Op Income | Net Income | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-28 | 321 | 192 | 52 | 34 | 0.66 |
| 2025-09-27 | 327 | 195 | 59 | 37 | 0.74 |
| 2025-12-27 | 339 | 202 | 54 | 39 | 0.70 |
| 2026-06-27 | 339 | 203 | 67 | 33 | 0.72 |

Key observations:
- Revenue grew from ~$297 (2023-07) to $339 (2026-06) — roughly +4–5%/yr, modest but consistent. FY-quarter cadence shows sequential growth each of the last four reported quarters ($321→$327→$339→$339).
- Gross margin improved markedly: ~47% in 2023 to ~60% in the latest quarter (203/339). This is the strongest structural signal — COGS fell from ~$155 to ~$137 while revenue rose.
- Operating margin ~17–20% in recent quarters vs. mid-single-digits a decade ago; the 2015–2017 losses (restructuring/divestiture era, EPS down to −$1.17/qtr) are well behind it.
- Latest quarter: Op income rose to 67 (+24% QoQ on a six-month gap basis) but net income fell to 33 vs 39 — implying below-the-line items (interest, tax, or one-offs) absorbed the operating gain. Worth flagging to a trader.

## Balance sheet — trajectory

| Period | Total Assets | Current Assets | Cash | Curr. Liab. | Equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-03-30 | 2,541 | 979 | 344 | 253 | 943 |
| 2024-12-28 | 2,462 | 900 | 296 | 548 | 879 |
| 2025-03-29 | 2,491 | 944 | 363 | 540 | 907 |
| 2025-09-27 | 2,396 | 835 | 245 | 283 | 849 |
| 2025-12-27 | 2,365 | 811 | 223 | 263 | 837 |

- Total assets peaked ~2,541 (Mar-2024) and drifted to 2,365 — modest balance-sheet shrinkage, consistent with debt paydown and buybacks rather than growth via acquisition.
- A notable current-liability spike (~540–578) in late-2024/early-2025 (likely debt reclassified to current) resolved by Sep-2025 (~263–283) — a refinancing/repayment event. Current ratio back to ~2.9 (811/263), comfortable liquidity.
- Cash declined from $363M to $223M over the period — funding deleveraging and/or buybacks. Equity also declined (943→837), consistent with buybacks exceeding retained earnings.
- Total liabilities not tagged by this filer; leverage must be inferred (Assets − Equity ≈ $1.53B, which includes deferred items, not just debt).

## Cash flow (periods are cumulative YTD; latest column is quarterly)

- Operating cash flow: FY-2025 (ended Mar-2026 proxy) — 9-mo Dec-2025: $222M vs prior-year pace of $193M (9-mo Dec-2024). Q1 FY-2027 (ended 2026-06-27): $52M OCF — solid.
- FCF: Q1 FY-2027 OCF $52M − capex $8M ≈ $44M. Capex has collapsed from ~$100M+/yr to a ~$15–20M/yr run-rate — the business is now very asset-light, boosting FCF conversion.
- Financing: −$52M in the latest quarter and −$79M/−$77M in prior periods — consistent net cash return (debt repayment/buybacks), not dilution.
- Historical context: the 2012 investing/financing spikes (−$570M / +$495M) were the big acquisition era; current profile is the opposite — generate cash, return/pay down.

## Actionable takeaways for traders
1. Margin story, not growth story: gross margin ~60% and capex down to ~5% of revenue drive FCF well above net income run-rate. Bullish quality signal.
2. Watch the below-the-line drag: latest quarter's net income fell despite record operating income — check the next filing for interest expense or one-time charges.
3. Balance sheet is being deliberately shrunk: cash down, debt-like liabilities down, buybacks active. Equity cushion ($837M) against ~$1.53B non-equity claims is adequate but not fat — a covenant/leverage check is warranted before sizing up.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for HAE (Haemonetics Corporation)

Let me open this debate by saying what the bears will try to hide behind: two weeks of price weakness. I'll take that head-on, because the story underneath is one of the cleanest quality transformations in mid-cap med-tech.

## The Fundamental Engine: This Is a Margin Story, Not a Hope Story

Forget vague "growth potential" narratives — HAE's numbers are filed with the SEC and they're excellent:

- **Gross margin: ~47% (2023) → ~60% (latest quarter).** That's not incremental improvement; that's a structural repricing of the business. COGS fell from ~$155M to ~$137M while revenue *grew*. Companies that expand gross margin 13 points get multiple expansion, not derating.
- **Operating margin at 17–20%** vs. mid-single digits a decade ago, with operating income hitting $67M last quarter — a record in this dataset, +24% over the prior reported period.
- **FCF inflection:** capex has collapsed from $100M+/yr to a ~$15–20M run-rate (~5% of revenue). The business is now asset-light. Last quarter: $52M OCF against $8M capex ≈ $44M FCF on $339M revenue — ~13% FCF margin quarterly.
- **Consistent top-line:** four consecutive quarters of sequential or flat-at-peak revenue ($321→$327→$339→$339), growing ~4–5%/yr on a ~$1.3B base.

The market already figured this out on 2026-08-18 — that's what a 15% gap-up on 4x volume means. Institutions didn't re-rate this stock on vibes; they re-rated it on the margin/FCF story I just described. Nothing in that story has changed since.

## The Technicals: A Correction in an Uptrend, Not a Breakdown

The bear will say "the stock is falling." Correct — and irrelevant, because context matters:

- Price sits ~35% above the 200-day SMA ($75.37). The 50-day is far above the 200-day. That's a textbook bull regime.
- The entire correction — $110.45 → $101.71 — is an ~8% pullback after a ~36% run since July. That is *normal* digestion, not deterioration.
- Critically: today's decline came on 625K shares — **average volume, not capitulation.** Distribution-grade selling pressure. If smart money were exiting, you'd see 1.5M+ share climactic days. You don't.
- Price is now pinned to the lower Bollinger Band ($101.26) directly atop the rising 50-day SMA ($100.26) — a stacked $1 support cluster that has *never been tested* since the August breakout. First tests of a rising 50-day after a gap-up re-rating historically resolve upward far more often than not.
- The setup is asymmetric: risk ~2 points to a stop below $99.7, target ~$105.5 (mid-band) — roughly 1:2 reward/risk — with the September plateau at $109–110 above that.

MACD below signal and RSI at 42? That's momentum *decay*, not trend flip — MACD is still positive territory, and RSI at 42 gives a bounce room without even needing oversold conditions. The bears are describing a stock that needs to fall; the indicators describe a stock that *can* rally at any moment.

## Preempting the Bear Arguments

**"Net income fell to $33M despite record operating income."** That's a below-the-line item — interest, tax, or a one-off — not business deterioration. The operating engine strengthened. I'll take record operating income with a financing/tax timing quirk over the reverse every time. Flag it, verify it next filing, but don't build a bear case on the line below the one that measures the actual business.

**"Cash declined from $363M to $223M and equity shrank."** That's deliberate capital allocation, not distress — the current-liability spike (~$578M) was refinanced/resolved to ~$263M, financing cash flow is consistently negative (paydown + buybacks), and the current ratio is ~2.9. A company shrinking its balance sheet while expanding margins is *returning* value, not losing it. Buybacks also mean every remaining share owns a bigger slice of a more profitable company — EPS accretion on top of margin gains.

**"No news, no sentiment signal, macro data missing."** Data gaps are not bearish evidence. Zero StockTwits chatter means HAE isn't a retail meme stock — it's institutionally owned, which is exactly why the August gap held. And I'll grant the news layer is a blind spot this week — which cuts both ways. You can't build a bear case on information that doesn't exist either.

**"A close below $100 breaks the structure."** Sure — and a bull case doesn't require pretending support can't break. It requires that the weight of evidence favors it holding. Record operating income, 60% gross margins, ~13% FCF margins, active buybacks, a rising-and-untested 50-day, non-capitulation volume on the pullback, and a 1:2 asymmetric setup — that's the weight of evidence.

## Bottom Line

HAE executed a structural margin transformation, got re-rated for it in August, and is now offering a pullback entry at the strongest technical support cluster in its chart, on declining (not accelerating) selling pressure, while fundamentals have only improved since. The bear case rests entirely on short-term price action and data absences; the bull case rests on filed financials and an intact primary uptrend. I know which one I'd rather own.

**Bullish bias on HAE above $100, targeting $105.5 then $109–110, with the structural story intact well beyond that.**
bear_history:
Bear Analyst: # Bear Case for HAE (Haemonetics Corporation)

The bull just gave you a beautiful story about margin transformation. I'll give him that — it's real, it's filed, and it's also **already priced in and then some**. The debate isn't whether Haemonetics is a better company than it was in 2023. It's whether you should pay $101.71 for it today, at ~35% above the 200-day, after the smart money already re-rated it and is now quietly heading for the exits.

## The Re-Rating Is Over — Now Comes the Payback

Let's look at what the bull's own timeline actually shows. The August 18 gap — $90 to $104.65 on 4x volume — was the market pricing in the *entire* margin story in one session. Institutions don't re-rate a stock 15% and then keep buying it forever; they re-rate it and then **distribute into the strength**. And what happened next? Price ground up to ~$110, stalled for five weeks, and has now bled lower for two straight weeks: $108.52 → $101.71, the weakest close since September 1.

That's not "digestion." That's what a topping pattern looks like in real time. Every rally since September 22 has been sold. The 10-EMA is above price and falling. MACD has been below signal since September 18 and the histogram just printed its most negative reading of the entire correction — momentum deterioration is *accelerating*, not stabilizing.

## Refuting the Bull Point by Point

**"Low-volume decline means no distribution."** The bull has this backwards. Yes, 625K shares isn't capitulation — but that's precisely the problem for him. The technical report says it plainly: "a genuine capitulation day on 1.5M+ shares would more likely mark a low." What we have instead is persistent, methodical selling on ordinary volume — institutional drift-down, the kind that continues for weeks because there's no panic wash to reset the tape. Low-volume declines don't bounce; they grind.

**"First tests of the rising 50-day resolve upward."** Sometimes. And when they don't, they resolve *violently*, because — and the bull conveniently skipped this — **the August 18 gap was never filled.** The zone below ~$102 was crossed in a single gap. There is essentially no technical support structure between the 50-day at $100.26 and the pre-gap region in the low $90s. A close below $100 doesn't trigger a measured pullback; it opens an air pocket. He's proposing you risk $2 to make $4 with maybe a coin-flip win rate. I'm telling you the downside tail isn't $4 — it's $10+ into an unfilled gap.

**"RSI at 42 gives room to bounce."** Read it the other way: RSI at 42 means the stock isn't even oversold. There is no rubber-band snapback condition here. Bears get *more* room to run before dip-buyers have any technical justification to step in. And a volatility squeeze just resolved to the downside — the Bollinger contraction from $28 wide to $8.5 broke bearish. Directional resolutions of squeezes are the moves that *trend*.

**"The margin story hasn't changed."** True — and irrelevant to price. Here's what the bull's own fundamentals table quietly admits: net income *fell* to $33M in the latest quarter despite record operating income. He waves that off as "below-the-line items." Fine — but he can't tell you what those items are, because the filing detail isn't in the report. Interest expense? Tax? One-off charge? The company generated $67M of operating income and shareholders saw $33M of it. Whatever ate the other half ate it *this quarter*, and nobody in this debate can rule out that it's recurring. Meanwhile cash dropped $140M, equity dropped $106M, and assets have been shrinking for a year. He calls that "deliberate capital allocation." It can equally be read as a company harvesting a mature business — shrinking the balance sheet because it has no growth opportunities worth funding. Capex at ~5% of revenue isn't just "asset-light discipline"; in a medical device company it's also **under-investment in future product cycles**. Plasma collection and hemostasis (TEG/ClotPro, NexSys) are competitive niches — Terumo, Haemonetics' plasma rivals, anticoagulant-free alternatives — and a company that starves capex and buys back stock is optimizing for the current multiple, not the next decade.

**"Growth of 4–5%/yr."** He said it himself. This is a low-single-digit grower trading 35% above its long-term mean *after* a full re-rating of the margin story. What's left to re-rate? The market has already paid for the margin expansion. From here, HAE needs multiple expansion on a mid-single-digit revenue grower in a rate environment we literally cannot verify — FRED data is unavailable, so the bull's whole case is implicitly unhedged against a rate shock to med-tech multiples he hasn't even measured.

## The Blind Spots Cut One Way: Down

The bull says missing news "cuts both ways." Wrong — it cuts asymmetrically against *him*. The sentiment layer returned zero retail interest, and two of three feeds were dark. There is no identifiable catalyst in the window. So ask: what lifts this stock from here? Not retail enthusiasm (zero). Not a visible catalyst (none surfaced). Not momentum (decaying). The only thing holding it up is the 50-day, which is *support by geometry*, not by buyers. Meanwhile, an FDA action, a guidance trim, or a plasma-collection capacity headline during a *data blackout* is exactly the kind of surprise that hits an unhedged, technically-vulnerable stock. You don't get to claim the blackout is neutral when your side needs good news and the tape is already rolling over.

## Bottom Line

- Short-term trend: bearish and accelerating into support; every rally sold for two weeks.
- The gap below ~$102 is unfilled — a break of $100 has air underneath it, not a floor.
- Net income divergence ($67M op income → $33M NI) is an unexamined leak the bull hand-waved.
- 4–5% revenue growth, shrinking balance sheet, ~5% capex — this is harvesting, not compounding.
- Zero sentiment signal, zero verified macro data, zero visible catalysts — the burden of proof is on the buyer.

The bull wants you to buy the first test of the 50-day at the top of a re-rating move, on a stock whose entire bull case was already priced in on August 18. I want you to wait: either the $100 level proves itself with actual reversal evidence, or it breaks and hands you the same company — which he concedes is genuinely better-run — $10 cheaper. **Bearish below $105.5; a close under $100 targets the mid-$90s gap-fill zone, and the risk/reward favors being early on the short, not the long.**

**Recommendation**: Underweight

**Rationale**: Both sides agree on the underlying facts — the margin transformation (47% → ~60% gross), record operating income, and the FCF inflection are real and filed. The disagreement is about whether those facts justify paying $101.71 today, and on that question the bear carried the stronger arguments. Three points decided it. First, the bear convincingly inverted the bull's risk/reward claim: the August 18 gap below ~$102 was never filled, so the 'risk $2 to make $4' framing understates the tail — a close under $100 opens an air pocket toward the mid-$90s, not a measured dip. Second, the tape agrees with the bear tactically: two weeks of methodical selling, every rally rejected, MACD histogram at its most negative reading of the correction, and a volatility squeeze that resolved downward — while RSI at 42 means there is no oversold snapback condition yet. Low-volume declines without a capitulation wash tend to grind rather than bounce.
